High level: we can support a weekend window but need to lock SLA and throttling. Our product requirement is that 99.9th percentile read latency on the serving path should not exceed 350ms for active customer traffic during the bulk run. If you can guarantee shard-level throttling that respects that bound for the production namespace pinecone-prod-435, we can sign off.

Technical ask for Dev: can you review the manifest and confirm whether prefix caching + warmed KV helps keep p99 under 350ms, and call out any risk vectors?

Marissa — I want commercial acknowledgement of any billable burst capacity credits and a statement of liability for degradation during the scheduled run. Also flag if this needs a formal amendment.

On Sat, Aug 29, 2026 at 11:05 AM, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com> wrote:
> Olivia — thanks for the quick run-through and the attachments.

Thanks — dug into the manifest briefly. A few quick notes from SRE/infra:

- Prefix KV caching: we should pre-warm the 10 most common prefixes per namespace. That reduces cold-miss p99 by ~60ms in our staging tests.
- Shard throttling: recommend a token-bucket limit per shard with a global rate cap. Start at 60% of measured ingest QPS for the past 7 days and ramp 10% every hour if p99 stays < 300ms.
- Fallback path: we should enable an S3 fallback for less-frequently-accessed vectors (cold tier) — new records can index to Pinecone, but any overflow should land in S3 to avoid headroom exhaustion.

I've attached the tuning snippet we plan to apply to the ingestion workers (ingestion_tune.yaml). Also: Sergio, please validate that we can instrument a canary route that runs 5% of live traffic through unchanged serving nodes during the run.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
